title: Congruence of probabilistic semantics
statement: Let $A$ be a randomized program with finitely many registers and deciders, let $O$ be an oracle, let $x$ be an input, let $G$ be a predicate on configurations, and let $a$ be an initial configuration. If the program has probabilistic semantics with parameter $p\in\mathbb{Q}$ from $a$ under $G$, and $p=q$, then it has probabilistic semantics with parameter $q$ from the same configuration under the same guard. Here probabilistic semantics means that every sequence of choices leads to termination while respecting $G$, and, for every number $N$ of random bits for which all length-$N$ choice sequences halt and satisfy the guard at each earlier live step, the probabilities of returning true and false are respectively $q$ and $1-q$.
hypotheses_covered: The program has probabilistic semantics with parameter $p$ under guard $G$
